transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, I'm here because... well, it's gotten to the point where other people are noticing it. My sister came over the other day, and she said I looked like I was moving underwater. And it's true, I mean, I feel like I'm dragging myself through molasses just to get out of a chair or answer a simple question. It takes me forever to just... respond, you know? Like my brain and my body are on a terrible delay. But then, on the flip side, sometimes I can't stop moving at all. I'll just be pacing back and forth in my apartment, back and forth, rubbing my hands together constantly. It's like I'm trying to shake off the adrenaline from a really bad customer service call, but the call ended hours ago, and I'm just stuck in this loop of restless energy and then absolute, heavy slowness. It's just exhausting, really, and I don't know why my body is doing this.
Do you feel like your mood changes along with these episodes of slowness and restlessness?

I... well, I don't really know if I can connect the two, to be honest. I mean, my mood is just... it's generally pretty low, you know? Like, a lot of the time, I just feel this heavy, gray sort of sadness that just kind of sits on my chest. But as for whether it changes exactly when I get all slow or when I start pacing around... I really haven't paid that much attention to the exact timing of it all. It's hard enough just trying to get through a shift at work, taking calls from people who are yelling about their internet bills, while I'm trying to figure out if I'm going to be stuck staring at my keyboard for ten minutes or if I'm going to have to get up and walk around the cubicle just to keep my skin from crawling off. So, I don't know if the sadness gets worse right when the slowness hits, or if the pacing makes me feel more down, or if they're just... happening at the same time. I just know I feel awful, but I couldn't tell you if they match up perfectly like that. I just haven't noticed a specific pattern with the mood and the moving, I guess. It's all just kind of a big, exhausting mess.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that you can't stop thinking about or feel compelled to repeat certain actions over and over?

I mean... no, not really. Not like... not like what you see on TV, you know? Where someone has to flip the light switch exactly five times before they can leave the room, or they have to wash their hands until they're raw. I don't have anything like that. I mean, sure, I double-check my locks sometimes, especially if I'm leaving for work and I'm already running late, which happens a lot lately because of the... the slowness I mentioned. I'll get halfway down the hall and think, "Wait, did I actually turn the deadbolt, or did I just think about turning it?" So I'll walk back and check. But that's just normal, right? Everyone does that. 

And as for thoughts... I mean, my thoughts can get pretty dark, obviously, with the sadness and everything. Sometimes I just sit there thinking about how pointless it all is, answering phones for a telecom company, getting yelled at for things I didn't do, and feeling like I'm just wasting my life. Those thoughts definitely loop around in my head a lot. But it's not like an obsession, I don't think. It's not a compulsion. It's just... it's just my reality right now. I don't feel forced to think about it; it's just what's there when I wake up and when I go to sleep. So, no, I wouldn't say I have those kinds of recurring, obsessive thoughts or actions. Just the regular kind of worrying and the heavy stuff that comes with feeling so down all the time.
Do you experience these periods of slowness and restlessness as distinct episodes, or are they more continuous?

Well, honestly, I think it's more like distinct episodes, but they bleed into each other so much it's hard to tell sometimes. But like I was saying earlier—and this is really why I made the appointment in the first place—it's become so obvious that other people can actually see it happening. It's not just in my head. Like, my sister pointed it out, and it made me realize how bad it's gotten. 

When the slowness hits, it's a very specific, heavy feeling. I'm literally moving like I'm underwater. It takes me forever just to answer a simple question or even push myself up out of a chair. It's like gravity has suddenly doubled in the room just for me. And then, completely out of nowhere, it switches. I'll get this restless phase where I'm just pacing back and forth across my apartment. My living room isn't even that big, but I'll just walk from the window to the kitchen counter, over and over, and I'll be rubbing my hands together constantly. It feels exactly like I'm trying to physically shake off the stress of a really awful customer service call—you know, when someone screams at you for twenty minutes about a late fee—but there's no call. It's just my body doing it. So they definitely feel like these intense, separate phases of either being totally weighed down or completely wired, even if they happen on the same day.
Do you notice any difference in your mood when you're experiencing one of these episodes of slowness versus when you're feeling restless?

I... well, I know I touched on this a little bit before, but... honestly, no, I don't really notice a difference in my mood between the two. It's not like... it's not like when I'm slow, I'm sad, and when I'm pacing, I'm angry or anxious or anything like that. I mean, I *am* anxious sometimes, but the mood itself, that heavy, gray sadness I was talking about? It just kind of stays there. It's like the background noise to everything else. 

Whether I'm sitting at my desk, staring at the screen for ten minutes trying to figure out how to type a simple email because my fingers feel like they're made of lead, or if I'm up and pacing around the living room, rubbing my hands together until they're red... the sadness is just there. It doesn't really shift or change its flavor, you know? It's just this constant, exhausting weight. I wish I could say, "Oh yeah, when I'm pacing, I feel super energized and happy," or "When I'm slow, I feel extra depressed," but it's really just the same awful feeling underneath it all. It's like the physical stuff—the slowness, the restlessness—is just happening on top of this big, dark cloud that never really moves. I just haven't noticed any kind of shift in how I feel emotionally when those physical things are happening. It's all just one big, continuous slump.
Are you having trouble keeping up with work or maintaining relationships with family and friends because of these episodes of slowness and restlessness?

Well, yeah, it definitely has an impact, though I guess I'm still functioning on some level. I mean, I can still keep a roof over my head, pay the rent on my apartment—usually on time, though sometimes I have to scramble at the last minute—but it's definitely taking a toll. Work is... work is getting really hard. I’ve just completely lost momentum with steady work. I’ll be sitting there, staring at the queue of incoming customer service calls, and I just... avoid them. I’ll put myself in 'after-call work' status for way too long because I just can't bring myself to pick up the headset. And I miss deadlines for the follow-up emails I'm supposed to send. My supervisor has pulled me aside a couple of times because I'm coming across as really unreliable. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I know how to do the job, but when the slowness hits, or when I'm just pacing around trying to shake off that restless feeling, I just can't focus on the customers. 

And as for my personal life... yeah, that's taken a hit too. I definitely see my friends a lot less than I used to. We used to go out and grab a beer or something on Fridays, but lately, by the time Friday rolls around, I'm just so exhausted from trying to force myself through the week that I make up some excuse to stay home. I just don't have the energy to sit at a loud bar and pretend everything is fine. Even just basic stuff is slipping. Like, my routines... making meals, running errands... it all just slides unless I absolutely force myself to do it. I used to love hiking on the weekends, going up to the trails just outside the city to clear my head, but I haven't done that in months. It's just too much effort. So, yeah, I'm still surviving, I guess, but I feel like I'm dropping the ball on pretty much everything else.
Are you feeling like you're losing relationships with friends and family due to your current condition?

Well, yeah, I guess that ties into what I was just saying about not seeing them as much. It's not just that I'm too tired to go out, though that's a big part of it. It's... it's actually causing some real friction when we do talk. My friends—and my sister too, actually, she brought this up last week when she called to check on me—they keep telling me that I sound really flat. Like, they say I'm hard to read now. 

I remember my friend Mark was telling me this whole long story about how he finally got that promotion he's been wanting for like two years, and I was happy for him, I really was, because I know how hard he worked for it. But apparently, my reaction was just... nothing. He actually stopped in the middle of talking and asked if I even cared. And I did! I just... I couldn't make my face or my voice show it. I ended up just giving him these really short, one-word answers, like "Cool," or "That's good." It’s like there’s a disconnect between what I’m feeling inside, or what I *should* be feeling, and what actually comes out. 

And because of that, because it's so exhausting to try and force myself to sound interested or to put on the right facial expressions, I just end up avoiding making plans altogether. It's easier to just stay in my apartment than to go out and have people look at me like I'm some kind of robot. So, yeah, I definitely feel like I'm losing those relationships, not necessarily because we're having big arguments, but because I'm just... fading out. I'm not giving them anything to work with anymore.
Are there any times when your symptoms of slowness or restlessness completely prevent you from doing anything at all?

Well... prevent me from doing anything at all? I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by "anything." Like, I don't think I've ever just laid in bed for three days straight completely unable to move a muscle, if that's what you're asking. But there are definitely these moments... these really weird, frustrating moments where I just get so overwhelmed by everything—the sadness, the heavy feeling, the restless energy—that my brain just kind of short-circuits, I guess? 

Like, the other morning, I was trying to get ready for work, and I was already running late because it took me forever just to put my shoes on. I went into the kitchen to grab my coffee, and I just... I stopped. I literally caught myself standing there, right in the middle of the kitchen floor, with my coffee mug halfway to my mouth. Just frozen. I wasn't thinking about anything specific, I wasn't daydreaming... I was just stuck there for I don't know how long. Maybe a minute? Maybe five? It felt like my body just forgot what it was supposed to do next. 

And then, on the flip side, when the restlessness gets really bad, I do this thing where I just walk the same little loop by the couch over and over again. Like, from the armrest, around the coffee table, back to the armrest. Just pacing that same tiny circle for no real reason. I'm not looking for anything, I'm not trying to get anywhere... I'm just doing it. And while I'm doing it, I'm not getting anything else done. I'm not answering emails, I'm not making breakfast, I'm just... stuck in that loop. So, I guess in those moments, yeah, it completely prevents me from doing what I'm actually supposed to be doing. It's like my body is doing something, but *I'm* not really doing anything, if that makes sense. It's just so bizarre, and it eats up so much time that I don't really have to spare right now.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yeah, it’s definitely been longer than two weeks. Honestly, it feels like it's been going on for a couple of months now, just this heavy, blank feeling that won't lift. You know, I used to have all these little things that made up my week, things that really made me feel like myself outside of work. Like, I’ve always been really into sketching. I have this nice leather-bound notebook I bought at this little independent art supply store, and I used to carry it everywhere with me. I'd just draw whatever caught my eye, people on the train, architecture, whatever. 

And I was super into coffee, too. Not just chugging it for the caffeine before I log into my customer service queue, but really getting into the actual tasting notes. I’d go to different local cafes and write down these detailed little coffee notes in a separate journal, comparing the different roasts, trying to pick out if it tasted like blueberry or cocoa or whatever. It sounds kind of pretentious when I say it out loud, but it was my thing, you know? That, and the weekend hikes I mentioned earlier. Those were the things that kept me grounded and made me feel alive. 

But lately... I just don't care about any of it. I'll literally sit at my kitchen table, open the sketchbook, uncap my pen, and I just... I just feel nothing pulling me toward it. I'll just stare at the blank page and feel completely empty. Or I'll force myself to sit on the edge of my bed on a Saturday morning and lace up my hiking boots because I know I *should* go outside, but then I just sit there. There's no spark, no motivation, no interest at all. It’s like the part of my brain that used to get excited about a new trail or a good cup of coffee just completely shut off. So I usually just end up untying the boots, taking them back off, and going back to doing absolutely nothing.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had an inflated sense of self-importance that lasted for at least one week?

Extremely happy? No... no, definitely not. I mean, honestly, I don't even remember the last time I felt just regular, everyday happy, let alone extremely happy for a whole week. Even before this whole heavy, blank phase started a couple of months ago, I was never really the type of guy to be bouncing off the walls or, you know, thinking I was on top of the world. 

As for the inflated sense of self-importance... yeah, no. I'm just a customer service rep, I've never walked around feeling like I was the smartest guy in the room or that I had some grand, special purpose. I just take my calls, log my tickets, and try to get by. 

And irritable... I mean, sure, I guess I get annoyed sometimes? Like, if a customer is screaming at me over the phone about a refund policy that I didn't even write, I get frustrated. Anyone would, right? But it's just a passing thing. It definitely doesn't last for a week straight. Once the shift is over, the annoyance is pretty much gone, mostly because I just don't have the energy to hold onto it. 

If anything, my problem right now is the exact opposite of everything you just asked about. I'm just so flat. The idea of having enough energy to be extremely happy, or to be that fired up and irritable about something for days on end... it honestly just sounds exhausting to even picture. I just don't have that kind of spark in me. I've always been pretty even-keeled, maybe a little on the quiet side, but never these huge, extended highs you're talking about. It's just never happened.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't need much sleep but still had a lot of energy?

No, I can't say I've ever experienced anything like that. Honestly, the idea of having a lot of energy without getting much sleep sounds like something out of a sci-fi movie to me. I mean, sleep is... well, it's a whole thing for me right now, but it's definitely not because I have all this extra energy to burn. 

Even back when I was younger, like when I was taking classes at the community college and trying to work at the same time, I always needed my solid eight hours. If I only got five or six hours because I was studying for a final or something, I'd be an absolute zombie the next day at work. I'd be dragging myself through every customer call, practically falling asleep at my headset. I never had those moments where I could just pull an all-nighter and then bounce into work the next day feeling completely fine and ready to take on the world. I know some people can do that, they just run on fumes and caffeine and somehow function perfectly, but that has never, ever been me. 

And lately, with everything feeling so heavy and blank, sleep is basically the only thing I *want* to do. It's not that I'm waking up at 3 AM feeling refreshed and ready to go for a run or clean the whole apartment. If I'm awake in the middle of the night, it's just because I'm lying there staring at the ceiling, feeling that weird restless energy I mentioned earlier, but it's not a *productive* energy. It's not like I feel energized, you know? It's more like my body is uncomfortable but I'm still completely exhausted. So, no, the whole "not needing sleep but having tons of energy" thing... I've never had a phase like that in my entire life. It’s pretty much always been the exact opposite.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you either felt depressed most of the day or had a markedly diminished interest in most activities?

Yeah, I mean... I feel like I kind of touched on this a minute ago, but yeah. It’s definitely been at least two weeks. Like I said, it’s been a couple of months now. And it’s not just a passing thing, you know? It’s not like I have a bad day at work where a customer yells at me, and I go home feeling bummed out, and then I wake up the next day and I’m fine. It’s... it’s constant. 

Most of the time since this whole thing started, that heavy, blank feeling has just been sitting right there. The sadness, and... well, this weird guilt I get sometimes about not doing anything, and the complete lack of interest in my sketching or my coffee notes or the hiking... it’s all just sort of humming in the background, all day, every day. And the sleep stuff, too, the waking up and staring at the ceiling. 

I mean, I guess there are some weeks where it feels a little lighter, maybe? Like, maybe the blanket over my head isn't quite as thick on a Tuesday as it was on a Monday, and I can at least manage to make a piece of toast without feeling completely overwhelmed by the effort of taking the bread out of the bag. But even on those "lighter" weeks, it’s still there. The baseline is still just... down. It never goes back to normal. It’s like the volume on everything good is turned all the way down, and the volume on the exhaustion and the emptiness is turned all the way up, and it’s just been stuck like that for months. So, yeah, absolutely, it's been well over two weeks of just feeling like this... most of the day, pretty much every day.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or irritable and engaged in activities that had potentially negative consequences, such as excessive spending or reckless behavior?

No, definitely not. I mean... excessive spending? I work in customer service, so my budget is pretty much calculated down to the penny every single month. I've never been the type to just go out and blow a paycheck on impulse. Actually, I'm usually the guy who stresses over buying a five-dollar coffee, you know? Like, I'll stand in the aisle at the grocery store comparing the unit price on two different brands of paper towels for ten minutes just to save forty cents. So the idea of going on some wild spending spree... it's just not in my DNA, let alone my bank account. 

And reckless behavior... I don't even know what that would look like for me, honestly. I've always been an incredibly cautious person by nature. Like, I'm the guy who double-checks that the front door is locked three times before I leave for my shift. I drive exactly the speed limit. I just don't like taking risks. 

Plus, like I was trying to explain earlier with the energy thing, you really need a certain amount of... of drive, I guess, to go out and do reckless things. You have to actually want to leave the apartment and go do something crazy. You have to have that kind of fire in you. But I just don't have that gear. Even before this whole heavy, blank phase set in a couple of months ago, my idea of a wild weekend was maybe trying a new trail for a hike on a Saturday morning and sketching a bit longer than usual. I don't drink much, I don't gamble, I've never gotten into any kind of trouble or done anything that would have negative consequences like you're talking about. 

I just... I can't even imagine waking up and feeling so fired up or agitated that I'd risk my savings or my safety. It just sounds completely exhausting, honestly. The sheer logistics of being reckless... I wouldn't even know where to start. You have to make plans, you have to go places, you have to interact with people in this highly charged way... it’s just not me. So, yeah, no, absolutely nothing like that has ever happened. I've always just kept my head down and played it safe.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and had a decreased need for sleep?

No, no, I... I feel like we're sort of circling around the same thing here, honestly. Like I was saying with the sleep and the energy before... I've never had a time where I felt extremely happy, or, you know, on top of the world, and just didn't need to sleep. That whole combination just doesn't happen for me. 

Even the irritable part... I mean, sure, I get annoyed sometimes, like if a customer is just completely unreasonable on the phone and won't listen to a single thing I'm saying about the company's return policy. That can make me irritable, absolutely. You sit there for forty-five minutes trying to explain something simple and they just yell at you... yeah, I get cranky. But it's not this... this extreme, buzzing kind of irritable where I'm pacing the floors and staying up all night. If I have a bad day like that, I want to sleep *more*. I want to just crawl under the covers and hide from the world, not stay up because I don't need the rest. 

And as for feeling extremely happy... I don't know, I've always been pretty even-keeled, I guess. At least until this heavy phase started. But even on my best days, back when things were normal and I was hiking and sketching and actually enjoying my coffee... I'd be content, you know? Happy, sure. Like, "Oh, the weather is perfect today and this trail is really quiet," kind of happy. But not this extreme, euphoric, vibrating kind of happiness where my brain just decides it doesn't need sleep anymore. 

Sleep has always been this fixed point for me. My body demands it. If I don't get it, I'm useless. So the idea of being so happy or so irritable that I just bypass the need for sleep entirely... it's just so far removed from anything I've ever experienced. I really can't emphasize enough how much I've always needed my sleep, and how right now, it's pretty much the only escape I have, even if it's broken up by lying there staring at the ceiling. So, no, never anything like what you're describing.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or unusually irritable for most of the day?

I feel like... I mean, didn't we just sort of cover this? I really don't mean to be difficult, but it feels like you're asking me the exact same thing again, just without the sleep part attached to it this time. And the answer is still no. I just... I don't have those kinds of extremes. 

I've never had a day, let alone a whole period of time, where I was just walking around extremely happy for most of the day. Like, what does that even look like for a normal person? Winning the lottery? The happiest I ever get—well, before this whole heavy, blank feeling set in a couple of months ago—was just... content. Like, I'd finish a really good sketch of a tree on my favorite trail, or I'd find a new roast of coffee at the store that was actually on sale, and I'd think, "Oh, that's nice." It's a quiet kind of good feeling. It's a mild satisfaction. It's definitely not this big, bright, all-day euphoria that you seem to be looking for. I'm just a very middle-of-the-road guy when it comes to being happy. 

And as for the irritability... like I was just saying a minute ago, sure, I get annoyed. Everyone gets annoyed. If I'm on hour six of my customer service shift and my headset starts cutting out with static, or if my neighbor decides to play his TV at maximum volume right when I'm trying to wind down, yeah, I'm going to be grumpy about it. I might sigh heavily, I might complain to myself while I'm making dinner. But it's a normal reaction to a specific, annoying thing, you know? It's not just this unusual, unprovoked irritability that takes over and lasts the whole entire day. Once the annoying thing is over—once I take the headset off or the neighbor turns the TV down—I just go back to my baseline. 

And lately, like I've been trying to explain, that baseline is just... flat. It's tired. It's sad. I don't swing up into extreme happiness, and I don't walk around furious at the world all day. I just sort of... exist under this heavy blanket. So, no, I really haven't ever experienced anything like what you're asking about. I just don't have those gears.
Have you ever had a distinct period of time where you felt abnormally happy or irritable?

I... I really don't know how else to say this, Doc. We are literally just going in circles now. It’s like... it's exactly like when I’m on the phone at work with a customer who keeps asking for a full refund after I've already explained, in three completely different ways, that their warranty expired two years ago. They just keep asking the same thing, hoping the answer is going to magically change if they phrase it slightly differently. I'm really not trying to be disrespectful here, I promise, but I feel like I've answered this exact question like three or four times in the last ten minutes. 

No. I have never had a distinct period of time where I felt abnormally happy, or abnormally irritable. 

I just don't get "abnormal" with my moods, unless you count this awful, heavy, empty phase I've been stuck in for the last couple of months. But before that? I've always just been a regular, boring, predictable guy. I wake up, I log into my customer service portal, I take my calls, I stick to my budget, I go to the grocery store, I make my dinner. There is no distinct period of time in my entire life where I was suddenly jumping on the furniture with joy or snapping at everyone in sight for no reason. I just don't have those massive swings in my personality. 

Like, just as an example, a few weeks ago, my landlord decided to have someone do construction right above my bedroom on a Saturday morning. Just hammering, drilling, right over my head at 7 AM. Was I annoyed? Yes, of course. Did I have a "distinct period of abnormal irritability"? No, I just sighed, put in my foam earplugs, tried to ignore it, and eventually just got up and made some oatmeal. I didn't lose my mind over it. I didn't go scream at the workers. I just dealt with it. 

And as for the happiness... I mean, I told you about the sketching and the hiking. That’s my absolute peak. Finding a quiet spot on a trail or getting the shading exactly right on a drawing of an oak tree. That’s it. That is the ceiling on my joy. There’s no secret, hidden chapter of my life where I was acting like a completely different, energized, euphoric person. It just... it doesn't happen. I really, honestly don't know how many other ways I can explain that I just don't get these extreme highs or angry spells you keep looking for. I'm just flat.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day?

Look, I... I don't even know what to say at this point. Adding "nearly every day" to the end of the question doesn't magically unlock a different answer for me. It's still no. It's been no the last three times, and it's no now. I really, truly do not get extremely happy or extremely irritable for most of the day, let alone nearly every day. 

If you want to know what "nearly every day" looks like for me, I can tell you exactly what it looks like, because it never changes. My alarm goes off at 6:45. I hit snooze once, maybe twice if I'm feeling particularly weighed down by that heavy feeling I told you about. I drag myself out of bed, I make a cup of coffee—usually just the store brand stuff lately because I haven't had the energy to go to the good roaster downtown—and I sit at my computer. I put on my headset. I log into the queue. I spend the next eight hours apologizing to people for shipping delays that I have absolutely no control over. I eat a turkey sandwich or maybe some leftover pasta on my lunch break. I log off. I sit on my couch. I might try to watch a show, but lately I usually just end up staring at the wall until it's an acceptable time to go back to sleep. 

That is my "nearly every day." There is no extreme happiness in that schedule. There is no buzzing, vibrating irritability where I'm snapping at people all day long. It's just... it's a very quiet, very gray routine. Even before this current slump, back when I was actually going out and hiking on the weekends, my days were just normal. Placid. Calm. I don't have these hidden weeks where I'm suddenly a completely different person, bouncing off the walls or raging at the world from sunrise to sunset. 

I don't know who you're looking for with these questions, but it's just not me. I'm sorry, I know you probably have a standard checklist you have to get through, but I really can't give you the answer you seem to be digging for. It's just a flat, absolute no.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely happy or irritable and had increased energy?

Okay, so now we're adding energy to the mix. Look, Doc... I mean, I really, truly do not know how to make this any clearer. We keep dancing around the exact same concept, just dressing it up in slightly different words. Increased energy? I can barely muster the energy to take my trash out to the dumpster at the end of the week. Like, the garbage truck comes on Friday mornings, right? So Thursday night I have to gather up the bags from the kitchen, and maybe empty the little bin in the bathroom, and honestly, lately, just looking at the plastic ties on the garbage bags makes me want to lie down on the linoleum and give up for the night. 

So, no. No extreme happiness with a side of boundless energy. No extreme irritability where I'm, I don't know, furiously scrubbing the baseboards or pacing holes in my apartment carpet because I'm just so charged up and mad. That is just not my life. 

Even when I was feeling okay, you know, before this whole heavy, blank slump set in, my energy was just... perfectly average. I'd have enough in the tank to finish my customer service shift, maybe drive out to the state park, walk a couple of miles, find a spot to sketch, drive home, and make a decent dinner. Like, I used to make this chicken stir-fry that took a lot of prep—chopping bell peppers, onions, broccoli—and that takes a normal amount of energy. But I wasn't running marathons. I wasn't staying up all night reorganizing my kitchen cabinets or whatever it is people do when they have this "increased energy" you're talking about. 

I don't get these surges. I don't have a high gear. I have a neutral gear, which was fine, and right now I'm stuck in a low gear where everything feels like dragging a boulder up a hill. But I have never, ever had a period where I was super happy or super angry and just buzzing with all this extra energy. I'm sorry, but the answer is still just no.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely happy or irritable and had increased energy, and if so, did it last for at least one week?

A week. Okay, so now we are adding a time minimum to the exact same question. Look, I... I’m really trying to keep my patience here, I really am, because I know you’re just doing your job and you have to be thorough, but... if I haven't had this happen for a single afternoon, or a single day, it definitely hasn't happened for an entire, uninterrupted week. 

I mean, think about how long a week actually is. A week for me is Monday through Friday, waking up to the same alarm, logging onto the same portal, dealing with the exact same angry people complaining about their tracking numbers not updating. And then Saturday and Sunday roll around, and right now, my weekends consist of me just trying to find the bare minimum willpower to maybe do a single load of laundry or wash the dishes that have been piling up. Like, I have this one pan, just a basic non-stick skillet that I usually use for eggs or whatever, and it’s been sitting in my sink since... I don't know, Tuesday? Because I just look at it and I can't bring myself to pick up the sponge. The sponge is right there, the dish soap is right there, and I just stare at it and walk back to the couch.
